label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
**Your money is stuck at Northvale. Here is everything we know.**

*Inês, Pinha team · Tuesday, 10 November 2026*

I'm going to start with the most important part, because some of you will only read the first lines.

**Your money is not lost.** It's held in a safeguarded account at Northvale Payments, separate from Northvale's own money. They can't use it, lend it, or spend it. But right now they also won't let anyone move it: not you, and not us.

**You can't withdraw today, and we can't fix that by ourselves.** We are working to move every euro to a new bank, Ostra Bank in Lisbon. Our estimate is 10 to 15 working days. That is an estimate, not a promise, and I'll explain why below.

**If you need your money urgently** for rent, medical costs, losing your job, or anything that can't wait, write to **urgent@pinha.example** with **URGENTE** in the subject. Those emails go to the front of the line.

**No monthly fee for November and December.** This applies to everyone, and you don't need to do anything.

Now the rest.

---

### What happened

Pinha doesn't hold your money directly. Like most savings apps, we work with a licensed payments partner, and for us that was Northvale Payments, an e-money institution based in Vilnius. Your round-ups and deposits went into their safeguarded account, and withdrawals came out of it.

On **Wednesday, 4 November**, Northvale emailed us to say they were ending our contract. They gave 30 days' notice. The only explanation was a "risk appetite review." We were already looking at options, because 30 days is tight but possible.

On **Friday, 6 November, at 09:00**, with no warning, they blocked all outgoing transfers. Deposits and round-ups stopped too. This goes directly against the 30 days of notice they had given us two days earlier.

That afternoon their account manager stopped answering our calls. Their phone line now goes to a voicemail in Lithuanian.

I've tried to find a fair word for this and I can't. Breaking the notice you gave, freezing thousands of people's savings and then disappearing is not "risk management." It's cowardice.

### What we're doing about it

**We complained to the regulators.** On Saturday, 7 November, we filed formal complaints with Banco de Portugal and with the Bank of Lithuania, which supervises Northvale. Rui, our CEO, has been on calls with lawyers and with Banco de Portugal every day since Friday. That's why I'm the one writing this instead of him.

**We already have a new partner.** We have signed with Ostra Bank in Lisbon. The plan is to move all balances there so you can use Pinha normally again, including withdrawals.

**Why we can't give you a date.** The move depends on two things we don't control:

1. Northvale has to send us the balances file, the official record of how much belongs to each person. Without it nobody can legally move the money.
2. Banco de Portugal has to approve the migration.

If both happen quickly, our estimate is 10 to 15 working days. If Northvale keeps dragging its feet, it will take longer. I'm not going to give you a date I can't stand behind. One false promise from a company this month is already one too many.

**Urgent cases.** We're asking Northvale and the regulators to release money individually for people in urgent situations, even before the full migration. I can't promise this will work for everyone. But we're pushing hard, and the more concrete your case is, the better our arguments are. Write to **urgent@pinha.example**, subject **URGENTE**, and tell us what's happening and what you need by when.

### Our part in this

I don't want this post to be only about Northvale. We made a mistake too.

We built Pinha on a single payments partner, with no backup. When things were going well that looked efficient. Now it looks naive, because it was. If we had a second partner already set up, this would be a bad week for us instead of a terrible one for you. That's on us, and we're changing it. Ostra will be our main partner, and we won't run with only one again.

And something personal. I'm a product designer, and I designed the screen in the app that says *"Your money is always yours. Take it out anytime."* I believed it when I wrote it. I look at it now and feel sick. The first part is still true: it's your money, nobody else's. The second part isn't true right now, and I'm sorry. We'll change that screen until it's true again.

### About the support emails

Since Friday we've received about 1,900 emails. We are three people answering them. Right now a reply takes around two days, sometimes more. I know that's too long when you're worried about your money.

We're reading all of them. Some of you are polite, and some of you are writing in capital letters. Both are fine.

On the metro this morning I read a message from a woman in Porto. She has saved for three years for the deposit on a car, and the dealer has given her until Friday to pay it. I nearly cried in front of strangers. If you're in a situation like hers, with a real deadline and real consequences, please use the URGENTE email so you don't get lost in the general queue.

### You're allowed to be angry

I'm not going to tell you to calm down. You trusted us with your savings, and right now you can't touch them. Be angry at Northvale, and be angry at us too, if you are. We're angry as well.

What I can do is make sure you're never left guessing.

### What happens next

- **Updates on this blog every Monday and Thursday** until this is solved. The next one is **Thursday, 12 November**. If something big happens in between, like Northvale sending the file or a regulator decision, we'll post the same day.
- **Don't delete the app or close your account.** Your balance is linked to your account, and keeping it open makes the migration simpler.
- **Your round-ups are paused**, so no new money is going into Northvale.
- **If you're in an urgent situation**, write to urgent@pinha.example with URGENTE in the subject.
- **For everything else**, email support as usual. We'll get to you, and we're sorry it's slow.

Your money is safe, and it is still yours. We're going to get it back to you, and we'll tell you the truth at every step until we do.

Inês
Product designer at Pinha, Lisbon

---

A few things to check before you publish:

1. **The date:** you said Tuesday 10 November, but today is Wednesday 11. If it goes out today, change the byline. "Next update Thursday 12 November" still works, it just becomes tomorrow.
2. **The word "cowardice":** I kept it because it's what you meant and it's justified by the facts. But Rui and the lawyers are already involved with Northvale, so it's worth a 30-second check with them that naming them this strongly in public is okay right now.
3. **The Porto user:** I left out her name, and the details are pretty generic. Still, if she might recognise herself, a quick "can I mention your story without your name?" email would be kind.
4. **"Don't delete the app / round-ups paused":** I added these as practical tips. Please confirm both are true for your setup.
5. **Something you might want to add:** a line like "We will never ask for your password or card details by email or phone." Scammers love situations like this one. Only add it if it's true for Pinha.
